intro: Xalapa is the capital of Veracruz, a hill city on the slopes of eastern Mexico's mountains, green with cloud forest and coffee. On its northern edge the Parque Lineal Río Sedeño follows a river, and beside its path stands a Mexican sycamore with a vast pale trunk mottled white and olive. A reader sent us its photograph, and puts the tree at about 150 years old.

trees.story:
A reader sent us this tree from the Parque Lineal Río Sedeño, the riverside park on the northern edge of Xalapa, and the photograph shows why they stopped on the path.

It is a Mexican sycamore, Platanus mexicana, a plane tree native to the mountains of eastern Mexico, and this one has grown to a size that makes the people walking past it look like children's toys. The trunk is the thing to see. It rises from a flare of thick roots like a pale column, its bark shedding in patches so that the whole surface is a map of white, cream and olive, as if it had been camouflaged. High up it opens into long white limbs, and the crown above them is hung with grey strands of moss. A bench stands at its foot, and the path runs right past.

The reader puts it at about 150 years old and its trunk at some six and a half metres round. Those figures are theirs, not a measurement we have seen. If you know the tree's history, or what the people of Xalapa call it, tell us here.

Walk round to the bench and sit with your back to the roots, then look straight up the trunk.
trees.how_to_recognise: Beside the park's earth path: a huge pale trunk patched white, cream and olive where the bark has shed, on a flare of thick roots, with a wooden bench at its foot and long white limbs hung with moss above.
trees.access: Free. On the path through the Parque Lineal Río Sedeño, a public riverside park.

faq.a: Yes. It stands beside the path in the Parque Lineal Río Sedeño, a free public park in Xalapa.
